question: A marketing team wants Claude to draft product descriptions in a specific brand voice and needs the tone and structure to stay consistent across many descriptions. What is the most reliable way to steer this drafting task?
options: A) Describe the brand voice in one adjective and let Claude infer the rest
B) Give no examples and repeat the word 'consistent' several times instead
C) Provide three to five diverse examples wrapped in tags that mirror the brand voice
D) Provide a single long example and ask Claude to make all future ones roughly similar
correct_answers: C) Provide three to five diverse examples wrapped in tags that mirror the brand voice
explanations: Incorrect. A one-word tone descriptor without examples leaves too much of the format and structure to be inferred rather than steered.
Incorrect. Repeating a vague adjective like 'consistent' does not give Claude concrete examples of the actual tone, format, or structure desired.
Correct. Using three to five relevant, diverse examples wrapped in example tags, few-shot prompting, is one of the most reliable ways to steer output format, tone, and structure.
Incorrect. A single example risks Claude picking up unintended, overly narrow patterns instead of generalizing the brand voice across varied product types.
